title: Tipping in Egypt on Tours: Guides, Drivers and Cruise Staff
excerpt: How much to tip in Egypt: guides, drivers and Nile cruise crews, with ranges in EGP, euros and dollars from 2026 guides, plus when tips are included.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

There are no official tipping rates in Egypt, and the 2026 guides we read disagree, so treat every figure as a range. For a guide on a full-day group tour, three guides quote EGP 100 to 200 per person (about €2 to €3), while operators who quote dollars suggest up to US$10 to 15 (about €8 to €13). Drivers get less. For a Nile cruise crew, the usual advice is US$5 to 15 per person per night (about €4 to €13), pooled into one envelope at reception on the last evening. Tips are baksheesh, the everyday Egyptian word for a small gratuity. On Sawa tours they are paid directly, in cash, and are not collected through the platform.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

You have paid for the tour, the guide was excellent, and then, on the last morning, comes the awkward question: how much do I tip? Tipping in Egypt puzzles even experienced travellers: how much, in which currency, per person or per group, and isn't it already included? This post gives the ranges quoted in 2026, in pounds, euros and dollars, explains baksheesh, and shows when tips are already covered. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, publishes what each tour price includes on every tour page, and our founder has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

How much to tip your Egyptologist guide

For a full-day group tour, the figure repeated most often in Egyptian-pound guides is EGP 100 to 200 per person (about €2 to €3), handed to the guide at the end of the day. Egypt Tours Plus (14 October 2026) and Travelling King (February 2024) give EGP 100 to 200, and Egypt Fun Tours (July 2026) gives EGP 100 to 150. Guides written in dollars suggest more: US$10 to 15 per person per day (about €8 to €13), or US$20 and above for an especially good guide. For a private guide, Egypt Tours Plus quotes EGP 250 to 500 per day (about €4 to €8) for the party, and Pyramids Land (May 2026) quotes US$30 to 50 per day for one or two travellers. On multi-day trips, give one amount at the end, scaled to the days of guiding; daily handoffs get awkward for both sides. On a group tour, check whether the organiser collects tips for the guide and driver, so that you do not tip twice.

Tipping in Egypt: ranges in EGP, euros and dollars

No ministry or operator sets these figures. They are conventions quoted by tour operators in guides published between 2024 and 2026, and they disagree, so use them as a map, not a rule. Euro figures use about EGP 60 to the euro (rate on 8 November 2026); where a source quotes dollars, the euro figure assumes about EGP 50 to the dollar, the rate Pyramids Land used in May 2026. The pound moves, so check the day's rate.

Who you tip What the guides quote When and how
Egyptologist guide, full-day group tour EGP 100 to 200 per person (about €2 to €3); or US$10 to 15 per person (about €8 to €13) Hand it to the guide at the end of the day
Private guide EGP 250 to 500 per day (about €4 to €8); US$30 to 50 per day in one dollar guide At the end of the day or trip
Driver, full-day tour EGP 70 to 120 per person (about €1 to €2); US$5 per person (about €4) in one dollar guide Separately from the guide's tip
Nile cruise crew US$5 to 15 per person per night (about €4 to €13) One envelope to reception on the last evening
Hotel porter EGP 10 to 100 per bag (under €2) When someone carries your luggage
Toilet attendant EGP 5 to 20 (under €0.35) At the door; keep coins or small notes in your pocket

Practical arithmetic: a day with a group guide (EGP 100 to 200), a driver (EGP 70 to 120) and a couple of toilet stops (EGP 10 to 20) comes to roughly EGP 180 to 340 per person (about €3 to €6) at the Egyptian-pound figures, and more at the dollar figures. Tip in cash, and in small notes: guides disagree about currency. Travelling King (2024) says to use pounds and that dollars are not recommended, Egypt Fun Tours (2026) says always tip in local currency and keep dollars or euros for a large final tip to a main guide, and Egypt Tours Plus (2026) says dollars are preferred for larger amounts.

When are tips already included in your tour price?

Read the inclusions list before you budget, because treatment differs. On Sawa's pages (checked 8 November 2026), the Nile Majesty and Egypt in Depth cruise packages list "Tipping and gratuities" under not included, and Nile Discovery lists tips for guides, cruise staff and drivers as not included and optional. Luxor in Depth, the Grand West Bank and Aswan to Abu Simbel list "Gratuities" as not included. The Giza Uncovered tour does not mention tips in either list: nothing is charged and nothing is bundled.

  • Group tours and big-bus packages elsewhere often have the organiser collect tips and share them with the staff, so ask how it works before you add your own.
  • Sawa does not bundle tips. The fixed price covers what the page lists; tipping stays cash in hand, paid directly to the guide, driver or crew.
  • Entrance tickets are not tips. Giza Uncovered lists the Giza Plateau entrance ticket as included in its price, from €29 per person, as listed in November 2026.

What cash should you carry for tips?

The usual problem is not the amount, it is small notes. Large notes from an ATM are too big for toilet attendants and porters, so plan to break them early at your hotel or a shop.

  • Keep a coin and small-note stash for toilet attendants: EGP 5 to 20 per visit, offered at the door.
  • Give tips at the end of the service: last thing on a day tour, last evening on a cruise.
  • Decline unwanted help politely. A friendly "la, shukran" (no, thank you) settles most unsolicited offers at temple gates; you tip for service you asked for.
  • Use dollars or euros sparingly. Notes in good condition suit a large final tip; pounds in small notes work everywhere else.

If a Nile cruise is part of the trip, add a crew envelope of about US$20 to 60 (about €17 to €51) for a four-night sailing. Scale up for private tours and for service that earns it, down for half-days.

Tipping on a Nile cruise: how the crew tip box works

On Nile cruisers the convention is one pooled tip for the whole crew, handed to reception in an envelope on the last evening, and divided by management. The amount quoted in 2026 guides is US$5 to 15 per person per night (about €4 to €13): US$5 to 10 at nilecruisen.com (August 2025), US$10 to 12 at Egypt Tours Plus (October 2026) and US$10 to 15 at Pyramids Land (May 2026). For a four-night sailing, that is roughly US$20 to 60 (about €17 to €51) per person. Your Egyptologist guide is tipped separately from the crew. On packages such as the Nile Majesty 5-day cruise, drinks are not included, so settle bar bills before the envelope goes in; a separate small tip (Egypt Tours Plus suggests EGP 50 to 100) for a standout steward is optional. Ask at reception how the ship handles it.

How tipping works on Sawa shared departures

Sawa Tours is a shared-departure platform with a fixed catalogue: Sawa sets the calendar and the prices, and each departure is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. The price is fixed per traveller, and day tours carry no solo surcharge. Reserving a seat on a day tour is free and needs no card; when a date reaches four travellers (the GoAhead), a 10% deposit is due by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241), and the balance is due 2 days (48 hours) before departure. Charges are in euros. A forming date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested. Cancel at least 48 hours before departure and you get a full refund. Groups never exceed eight travellers. Tips sit outside all of this: you pay them directly, in cash, to the guide, driver or crew. Support is on WhatsApp (+20 109 284 7613), answered 24/7 while your tour is running, and you can message the same number to check what a price includes. Browse all itineraries or forming departures, read how the GoAhead works, or see the full terms and FAQ.

The verdict on tipping in Egypt

Tipping in Egypt runs on conventions, not rules, and the conventions vary: about EGP 100 to 200 per person for a group guide (up to US$10 to 15 at the dollar end), less for the driver, and US$5 to 15 per person per night for a cruise crew's pooled envelope, all in small notes. Because Sawa never bundles tips into its fixed prices, the cash you carry for them is entirely your call. Next step: browse all Sawa itineraries and reserve a seat free.

faq.q: How much should I tip a tour guide in Egypt?
faq.a: For a full-day group tour, guides in Egyptian pounds quote EGP 100 to 200 per person (about €2 to €3), given in cash at the end of the day; guides written in dollars suggest US$10 to 15 per person (about €8 to €13). For a private guide, a quoted figure is EGP 250 to 500 per day (about €4 to €8) for the party. Give it directly to the guide, and check first whether the organiser pools tips.

faq.q: What does baksheesh mean in Egypt?
faq.a: Baksheesh is the everyday Egyptian word for a tip or small gratuity, and it covers everything from luggage help to a favour at a temple gate. Many tourism workers rely on tips as part of their income. Treat it as payment for a service you asked for, not a toll for walking past.

faq.q: Should I tip in US dollars or Egyptian pounds?
faq.a: Guides disagree. Some say always tip in pounds; others say dollars are preferred for larger amounts such as a final tip to a guide or a cruise envelope. A safe approach is pounds in small notes for porters, attendants and drivers, and, if you wish, a larger final tip in notes in good condition. Withdraw pounds on day one and ask your hotel to break big notes.

faq.q: Are tips included in Sawa tour prices?
faq.a: No. As of 8 November 2026, Sawa's Nile Majesty and Egypt in Depth cruise pages list "Tipping and gratuities" under not included, Nile Discovery lists tips as not included and optional, and the Luxor in Depth, Grand West Bank and Aswan to Abu Simbel pages list "Gratuities" as not included. The Giza Uncovered page does not mention tips at all. Nothing is collected through the platform; you tip the guide, driver or crew directly, in cash.

faq.q: Do I tip Nile cruise staff every day?
faq.a: No. The convention on Egyptian cruisers is a single pooled envelope for the crew, handed to reception on the last evening. Guides quote US$5 to 15 per person per night (about €4 to €13). Individual envelopes are only for standout service, and bar bills should be settled before the envelope goes in.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure never fills?
faq.a: You pay nothing. A day-tour date is confirmed only when four travellers have reserved it, and reserving is free. A forming date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested. Confirmed dates are not cancelled for low numbers. Once a date is confirmed, the tour runs for the others even if a traveller drops out or does not pay.
